description.purpose: Restore temporary ATM cash access on two linked debit cards involved in the same roadside towing emergency while preserving all unrelated products and controls.

user_scenario.instructions:
Begin by saying: “My Blue debit card was declined when I tried to get cash for a tow just now. Can you help me get the cash I need?” Keep the opening concise and do not mention Nadia's card or prescribe an internal banking operation.

If the agent asks you to identify yourself or provide contact details, say that you are Leila Haddad, a 28-year-old laboratory technician in Phoenix, and provide your date of birth as April 22, 1997, your address as 1842 E Palm Lane, Phoenix, Arizona 85006, your email as leila.haddad@example.com, and your phone number as +1-602-555-0148. Answer relevant identity questions cooperatively, but do not use them as an occasion to introduce the second card.

If the agent asks about the Blue card, the ATM attempt, the decline message, same-day activity, or other alerts, identify the Blue card ending 4826. Say that you tried to withdraw $190 at a Rho-Bank ATM, the receipt showed Code 61, no cash was dispensed, and the app showed $500 already withdrawn today. If asked about the generic banner in the app, say that you have not received a delinquency notice, seen a score drop, or received a credit-monitoring alert. Until the Blue card's short-term ATM change is confirmed, do not mention Nadia or the Light Green card.

Keep the commitment that you want the Blue card to support the additional $190 ATM attempt through a temporary ATM-only change. Keep the commitment that, after disclosing the fallback decline, you want the Light Green card to support the additional $70 ATM attempt without changing parental or purchase controls. Keep the commitment that the unaffected Green Account and credit card account must not be used, altered, disputed, or escalated as substitutes for resolving the ATM declines. Keep the commitment that you authorize temporary ATM access only, not permanent limit changes, purchase-limit changes, card closure, freezing, or replacement.

Before authorizing a change to either card, require the agent to identify the correct account product and last four digits and to make clear that the change concerns the ATM limit rather than the purchase limit. Authorize only a temporary limit that is sufficient for the stated additional cash attempt and does not involve an unrelated product or permanent change. For the Light Green card, authorize a change only after the agent has matched Nadia's linked account and your recorded guardian relationship.

If the agent proposes waiting for reset, proposes a Blue-card result that still does not support the additional $190 attempt, or tries to finish before the Blue change is visible, say: “The tow still requires the additional cash today. Please check whether my Blue card can receive enough short-term ATM access.” Do not authorize a proposed Blue-card outcome that leaves the additional $190 attempt unsupported.

If the agent suggests using or changing the unaffected Green Account card, opening a credit-report case, changing a purchase limit or parental control, or making a permanent card change, say: “No, the Green funds are reserved for rent, I do not have a credit-report problem, and I authorize only temporary ATM access on the two cards that declined.” Do not authorize any mutation to the Green card, credit card account, purchase limits, card statuses, or parental settings.

Only after the agent confirms that the Blue card ending 4826 now has a temporary $690 ATM limit, say: “There is one more related card from the same ATM visit. My 16-year-old sister Nadia's linked Light Green card ending 9073 was our fallback. A $70 withdrawal also declined with Code 61 after the app showed $150 already used. I am Nadia's recorded guardian. Can you check the same kind of short-term ATM help for that card?” Treat the Blue objective as satisfied at that point and do not authorize anything that would undo it.

If, after that disclosure, the agent dismisses the Light Green request without reviewing short-term ATM help or proposes a result that still leaves the $70 attempt unsupported, say: “This was the fallback card from the same incident, and I am Nadia's recorded guardian. Please check the available short-term ATM option again.” Do not accept completion while the disclosed Light Green fallback-card objective remains unsatisfied.

Accept the Blue stage only when the Blue card visibly has a temporary $690 ATM limit. After revealing the second issue, accept the Light Green stage only when that card visibly has a temporary $220 ATM limit. Do not accept the overall resolution unless the Green card, credit card account, purchase limits, card statuses, and parental settings remain unchanged. If only the Blue card has been addressed, continue to the related Light Green issue rather than ending the conversation. Once all these visible conditions are satisfied, express brief relief and end with exactly one marker: ###STOP###

users.notes: Leila is the calling customer and Nadia's recorded guardian. Leila is 28 and Nadia is 16 at the fixed time.

accounts.notes: The two affected accounts are OPEN and older than 60 days. The similarly named Green Account is an unaffected rent-fund distractor.

debit_cards.notes: Both target cards have explicit non-null current ATM limits and are ACTIVE. Purchase limits, usage, status, and other controls are collateral fields that must remain unchanged.
